# 1 Samuel Chapter 25 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 164v–165v | **Source Image:** 1SA_025_page_001.jpg, 1SA_025_page_002.jpg, 1SA_025_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Samuel died, and all Israel gathered to mourn for him. They buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David moved down to the wilderness of Paran.

**2** There was a man in Maon who had property in Carmel. He was very wealthy — three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. He was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

**3** His name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigail. She was intelligent and beautiful. He was harsh and mean — a Calebite.

**4** While in the wilderness, David heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.

**5** He sent ten young men with these instructions: "Go up to Carmel, find Nabal, and greet him in my name.

**6** Say to him: 'Long life to you! Peace to you, peace to your household, and peace to everything you own.

**7** I hear you're shearing. When your shepherds were with us, we never mistreated them, and nothing of theirs went missing the whole time they were in Carmel.

**8** Ask your own men — they'll confirm it. So please be generous to my men, since we've come at a good time. Give whatever you can to your servants and to your son David.'"

**9** David's men delivered the message and waited.

**10** But Nabal snapped at them: "Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? The country is full of servants running away from their masters these days.

**11** Why should I take my bread, my water, and the meat I've slaughtered for my shearers and give it to men I've never even heard of?"

**12** David's men turned around and went back, and they reported every word.

**13** David said to his men, "Strap on your swords!" They all armed themselves — David included. About four hundred marched out with David, while two hundred stayed behind with the supplies.

**14** Meanwhile, one of Nabal's servants told Abigail: "David sent messengers from the wilderness to pay respects to our master, and he screamed at them.

**15** But those men were very good to us. We were never harassed, and nothing went missing the whole time we were out in the fields with them.

**16** They were like a wall of protection around us, day and night, the entire time we were herding sheep near them.

**17** Think about what you can do, because disaster is hanging over our master and his whole family. He's so nasty that no one can even talk to him."

**18** Abigail moved fast. She gathered two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five dressed sheep, five measures of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred fig cakes, and loaded everything on donkeys.

**19** She told her servants, "Go on ahead — I'll be right behind you." She said nothing to her husband Nabal.

**20** As she was riding her donkey down a mountain path, David and his men came around the bend heading toward her.

**21** David had just been saying, "What a waste — guarding everything that man owns in the wilderness so that nothing went missing, and he pays me back with contempt!

**22** May God deal with me severely if I leave a single male alive in his household by morning!"

**23** When Abigail saw David, she quickly dismounted and fell facedown before him.

**24** She fell at his feet and said, "My lord, let the blame fall on me alone. Please, let me speak — hear what your servant has to say.

**25** Please don't pay any attention to that worthless man Nabal. He's exactly what his name says — 'Fool' is his name, and foolishness follows him everywhere. I myself never saw the men you sent.

**26** Now, my lord — as surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live — the LORD has kept you from bloodshed and from taking vengeance with your own hands. May your enemies and all who mean you harm end up like Nabal.

**27** Here is a gift your servant has brought for my lord. Let it be given to the young men who follow you.

**28** Please forgive your servant's boldness. The LORD will certainly establish a lasting dynasty for my lord, because you fight the LORD's battles, and no wrongdoing will be found in you as long as you live.

**29** Even if someone pursues you and seeks your life, your life will be held secure by the LORD your God, kept safe like a treasure in his pouch. But the lives of your enemies he will hurl away like stones from a sling.

**30** When the LORD has done for my lord everything he promised and has made you ruler over Israel,

**31** you won't want this on your conscience — the staggering burden of needless bloodshed and of having taken revenge with your own hands. And when the LORD has blessed my lord, remember your servant."

**32** David said to Abigail, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me today!

**33** And praise your good judgment — and praise you yourself — for keeping me today from bloodshed and from avenging myself with my own hands.

**34** Because as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives — the God who has kept me from harming you — if you had not come to meet me so quickly, not one male in Nabal's household would have been alive by morning."

**35** David accepted what she had brought him and said, "Go home in peace. I have heard you and granted your request."

**36** When Abigail returned to Nabal, she found him throwing a banquet fit for a king. He was in high spirits and very drunk, so she told him nothing until morning.

**37** In the morning, when Nabal had sobered up, his wife told him everything. His heart failed him and he became like a stone.

**38** About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal and he died.

**39** When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Praise the LORD, who has upheld my cause against Nabal's insult and has kept his servant from doing wrong! The LORD has brought Nabal's evil back on his own head." Then David sent word to Abigail, proposing marriage.

**40** David's servants went to Abigail at Carmel and said, "David has sent us to take you to be his wife."

**41** She bowed facedown to the ground and said, "Your servant is ready to wash the feet of my lord's servants."

**42** Abigail quickly mounted a donkey and, attended by five of her maids, went with David's messengers and became his wife.

**43** David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel. Both women became his wives.

**44** Saul had given his daughter Michal — David's wife — to Palti son of Laish, from Gallim.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **25:1 — Samuel's death**: One sentence for the passing of a giant. Samuel's death is wedged between chapters as an almost casual notice, but it marks the end of an era. The man who anointed both kings is gone. From here on, the story belongs to David alone.

2. **25:3 — "his name was Nabal"**: The narrator is not subtle. Nabal means "fool," and the text tells you his character matches his name before the story even begins. The question isn't whether he'll self-destruct — it's how.

3. **25:29 — "the bundle of the living"**: Abigail's speech reaches its theological peak here. The image of God keeping David's life secure — "bound in the bundle of the living" — became one of the most beloved Jewish memorial phrases. She is speaking as a prophet, not just a diplomat.

4. **25:32-34 — David's near-miss**: David was minutes away from a massacre. Abigail intercepted not just a military column but a moral catastrophe. David recognizes this immediately — she saved him from the one thing that could have disqualified him from the throne: innocent blood on his hands.

5. **25:44 — Michal given away**: A devastating footnote. While David gains Abigail, the narrator reminds us that Saul has given away David's first wife, Michal — the woman who saved David's life. This act of spite will have consequences that echo through 2 Samuel.

— PNEUMA
